raw_response:
I'm 46, been farming these 6 mu since I was 16. I only finished primary school, but I know my land better than any book. Four mu I do wheat then maize — that's the rotation my father taught me, and I won't mess with it. The other 2 mu I grow stevia. I started that three years back after my neighbor Old Zhang at the east end of the village made good money selling dried leaves to the collection station.

For my wheat on the 4 mu: Last year I put one 50kg bag of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer per mu as base fertilizer at sowing, and I got 500 kilos per mu. This year I'll do the same — one bag per mu mixed in when I rotary till after the maize stalks are chopped. That compound costs me over 200 yuan a bag now, but I need it. In March when the wheat turns green, I spread half a bag — 25 kilos — of urea per mu. That's another 60-odd yuan per mu, but my father always said wheat is hungry in spring. I irrigate three times: once before winter if the weather is dry, once at jointing around April, and once at grain filling in May. Two pesticide sprays: herbicide when the wheat is small, and fungicide when it heads out. I expect about 520 kilos per mu if the weather holds.

For maize on the same 4 mu: Right after wheat harvest in early June, I hire the seeding machine to plant directly into the wheat stubble — no tilling, no time to waste, and the soil is loose enough. I put 40 kilos of compound fertilizer per mu through the planter. When the plants are knee-high, about two weeks later, I spread 25 kilos of urea per mu. I irrigate twice: once at tasseling if it's dry, and once at grain filling. Two pesticide sprays, one for weeds and one for corn borer. I usually get about 600 kilos per mu.

For my 2 mu of stevia: I rotary till in April and make flat beds. I put 50 kilos of compound fertilizer per mu as base. After the first cutting in July, I top-dress with 20 kilos of urea per mu. Stevia drinks more water than grain crops, so I irrigate four times through the season. I spray pesticide three times because aphids love stevia leaves and ruin them. I cut and dry the leaves, and I expect about 140 kilos of dried leaves per mu.

My wife and I do almost all the work ourselves. I only hire the combine for wheat and maize harvest, and sometimes hire one worker at stevia cutting time. Fertilizer is my biggest cash cost — every bag is real money. But I've seen what happens when you skimp: the plants turn yellow and the yield drops. A bad harvest means my daughter's school fees are in trouble. So I'd rather put a little too much than too little. I watch what Old Zhang and the others around me do. If they add more, I think about adding more. If they cut back, I cut back slowly, because change is risky.
